svg.aria-label: Diagram: how Partner Interconnect differs from Dedicated in Google Cloud; it requires separately obtaining services from a third-party network service provider, and suits a data centre that cannot reach a Dedicated colocation facility or needs that do not warrant a whole 10-gigabit connection, with VLAN attachment capacity ranging from 50 megabits to 50 gigabits and priced per attachment on that capacity; the Layer 2 versus Layer 3 split where Layer 2 means you configure and establish BGP between your Cloud Routers and your on-premises routers for every attachment while Layer 3 means the provider establishes it and you configure no BGP locally; pre-activation being available only on Layer 3 because its BGP is fully automated, and the fact that ordinary activation exists precisely to let you confirm you are connected to the provider you expected, so pre-activating trades away that identity check; the availability tiers counted in VLAN attachments rather than circuits, with 99.9 percent needing two attachments in one region in separate edge availability domains from the same provider in one metro, and 99.99 percent needing four attachments two per region across two metros with two Cloud Routers and the VPC network in global dynamic routing mode; the reason edge availability domains matter being that maintenance windows are coordinated between domains inside a metro but not across metros; and above all that Google's SLA covers only the link between your VPC network and the provider's network, not between the provider and you
svg.title: Partner Interconnect: the nines stop at the provider's edge
svg.text: Same console, same attachments, same nines on the label — a different promise underneath.
#87 bought circuits. Here a third party owns them, and the SLA stops where they begin.
Read this before quoting a number to anybody
Google’s SLA applies ONLY to connectivity between your VPC network and the SERVICE
PROVIDER’S network. It does NOT include connectivity between YOUR network and theirs.
An end-to-end number exists only if your provider offers its own SLA on top of a
Google-defined topology. That is a question for them, and it is worth asking in writing.
When Partner is the right door
Your data centre cannot reach a Dedicated colocation facility, OR your needs do not
warrant an entire 10-Gbps connection. It requires a third-party provider, separately.
Attachment capacity: 50 Mbps to 50 Gbps — a floor 200x below a 10-Gbps circuit, and
each attachment is priced on its capacity.
LAYER 2 — the BGP is yours
• YOU configure and establish the BGP
session between your Cloud Routers and
your on-premises routers
• Once per VLAN attachment
• The config details come FROM the
attachment, after the provider sets it up
• No pre-activation
LAYER 3 — the BGP is theirs
• The PROVIDER establishes the BGP
session between your Cloud Routers and
THEIR on-premises routers
• You configure NO BGP locally
• Google and the provider set the correct
configuration automatically
• Pre-activation is available
What activation is actually for — and what pre-activation gives up
ACTIVATION LETS YOU CHECK THAT YOU’RE CONNECTING TO AN EXPECTED SERVICE PROVIDER.
So the manual step is an identity check, not paperwork. Pre-activate and the attachment
passes traffic the moment the provider configures it — with nobody confirming who that was.
99.9% — counted in ATTACHMENTS
• At least TWO VLAN attachments in a
SINGLE region
• In SEPARATE edge availability domains
• The SAME provider for both
• Both in ONE metro
• At least one Cloud Router on both
99.99% — two regions, no exceptions
• At least FOUR attachments, TWO PER
REGION
• Two regions even if your VMs are all
in ONE region
• Each pair its own Cloud Router
• One metro per region, two metros total
• Routing mode MUST be global
Why edge availability domains are the unit that matters
MAINTENANCE WINDOWS ARE COORDINATED between different edge availability domains within
the SAME metro — and NOT coordinated across different metros.
That single fact explains the whole shape of both topologies: domains protect you from
planned work, metros from everything else.
API TRAP: the console assigns connections and edge availability domains for you. The API does not.
